items.question: Who utters the curse that Micah heard?

window_text.1: Now a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim
window_text.2: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have that silver with me; I took it.” Then his mother said, “The Lord bless you, my son!”

items.original_question: Who utters the curse that Micah heard?

blind.question: Who utters the curse that Micah heard?

readings.support: said to his mother, | I heard you utter a curse

assessments.reason: Micah says to his mother, “I heard you utter a curse,” so the “you” is his mother, matching the key.

blind.reason: Micah addresses his mother and says he heard “you” utter a curse, identifying the curser as his mother.

editor.quote: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse
editor.contrast: Micah’s mother uttered the curse; Micah heard it rather than uttering it.
editor.reason: A reader could confuse the speaker with the person who cursed, but Micah is addressing his mother as “you” and says that he heard “you utter a curse,” uniquely identifying his mother.

reader.quote: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse
reader.contrast: Micah’s mother, the person addressed as “you,” versus Micah, the speaker.
reader.reason: Micah is speaking to his mother and says that he heard “you” utter the curse, so the key is fully supported. The question clearly tests who performed the action within the quoted speech.

items.question: Who is expected to make the image in the mother’s vow?

window_text.3: When he returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, she said, “I solemnly consecrate my silver to the Lord for my son to make an image overlaid with silver. I will give it back to you.”
window_text.4: So after he returned the silver to his mother, she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who used them to make the idol. And it was put in Micah’s house.

items.original_question: Who is expected to make the image in the mother’s vow?

blind.question: Who is expected to make the image in the mother’s vow?

readings.support: for my son to make an image

assessments.reason: The vow explicitly says, “for my son to make an image,” indicating the son is expected to make it.

blind.reason: The passage states “for my son to make an image,” matching the key’s answer of her son.

editor.quote: for my son to make an image overlaid with silver
editor.contrast: The son is the expected maker named in the vow, while the silversmith is the person who later actually makes the idol.
editor.reason: The later mention of the silversmith makes that alternative plausible, but “in the mother’s vow” directs the reader to her quoted words, where “my son” is the one assigned to make the image.

reader.quote: for my son to make an image overlaid with silver.
reader.contrast: The son named in the mother’s vow versus the silversmith who later actually makes the idol.
reader.reason: The vow explicitly assigns making the image to her son, while the next verse reports that she gave the silver to a silversmith who made it. Resolving the question requires keeping the vowed agent distinct from the later actual craftsman.

items.question: Who serves as priest for Micah?

window_text.5: Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household gods and installed one of his sons as his priest.
window_text.6: In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.

items.original_question: Who serves as priest for Micah?

blind.question: Who serves as priest for Micah?

readings.support: installed one of his sons as his priest

assessments.reason: The passage states Micah "installed one of his sons as his priest," which matches "one of Micah’s sons."

blind.reason: The text explicitly says Micah made one of his sons his priest, matching the key.

editor.quote: installed one of his sons as his priest.
editor.contrast: Micah, the shrine owner who appoints the priest, versus one of his sons, who serves as priest.
editor.reason: The wording directly asks who holds the priestly role. The passage distinguishes Micah as the person making the appointment from his son as the appointee, ruling out Micah as the priest.

reader.quote: installed one of his sons as his priest
reader.contrast: Micah is the person who appoints the priest; one of Micah’s sons is the person who serves as priest.
reader.reason: The window directly assigns the priestly role to one of Micah’s sons, so the key is complete and unambiguous. The question tests the distinction between the person installing the priest and the person installed.

items.question: From which place does the young Levite set out?
items.answer: The young Levite leaves from Bethlehem in Judah.
items.competitor: The young Levite leaves from Micah’s house in the hill country of Ephraim.

window_text.7: A young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, who had been living within the clan of Judah,
window_text.8: left that town in search of some other place to stay. On his way he came to Micah’s house in the hill country of Ephraim.

items.question: In whose house does the young man live?
items.answer: The young man lives in Micah’s house.
items.competitor: The young man lives in the young man’s house.

window_text.9: Micah asked him, “Where are you from?” “I’m a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” he said, “and I’m looking for a place to stay.”
window_text.10: Then Micah said to him, “Live with me and be my father and priest, and I’ll give you ten shekels of silver a year, your clothes and your food.”
window_text.11: So the Levite agreed to live with him, and the young man became like one of his sons to him.
window_text.12: Then Micah installed the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.
window_text.13: And Micah said, “Now I know that the Lord will be good to me, since this Levite has become my priest.”

items.original_question: In whose house does the young man live?
items.original_answer: The young man lives in Micah’s house.

editor.quote: “Live with me and be my father and priest
editor.contrast: Micah’s house versus the young man’s own house.
editor.reason: Although “his house” could locally appear to refer to the young man, Micah invited him to live with him, and the Levite agreed. The context therefore resolves the house as Micah’s. The question meaningfully tests pronoun and ownership reference.

reader.quote: Then Micah installed the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.
reader.contrast: Micah’s house versus the young man’s own house.
reader.reason: The surrounding lines say that the Levite agreed to live with Micah, became like Micah’s son, and became Micah’s priest. Thus “his house” refers to Micah’s house. The question clearly tests resolution of that possessive reference rather than mere fact retrieval.
